Definition: Zered, a brook East of the Dead Sea
BiblicalUsage: Zered is the brook Israel crossed near the end of the wilderness years, and the crossing marks a turning point. At the brook Zered the generation that had rebelled was gone, and the new generation stepped toward the land. The place itself is named only for the crossing — a brook that closes one chapter and opens the next.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God marks His turning points in geography: a brook crossed, a generation buried, a promise still standing on the other side.
